land.text: Bima and eastern Sumbawa, turned into a Dutch fief (leen) in 1905

successors.note: The page: 'In 1905 Bima was turned into a "fief" (leen) and Sultan Ibrahim had to give up the rights to foreign trade'; indirect colonial rule ran 'from 1908 to 1949', the sultanate 'ceased to be a sultanate in 1958' (absorption into Indonesia 17 August 1958). Bima was a 'subordinated ally of the VOC' from 8 December 1669: the ledger carries it as vassal events (dutch-republic 1669-1799, dutch-east-indies 1800-1905). Cliopatria's Dutch East Indies shape already covers part of eastern Sumbawa from 1800.

ledger.note: 1626: Sumbawa under Makassar. 'Sumbawa was attacked through three expeditions in 1618, 1619, and 1626'; Bima's king had 'signed a contract of alliance with Makassar' (undated) and 'A rebellion against his Makassarese-backed rule took place in 1632-33'. The page does not call Bima a vassal and names no tribute; the year is the last expedition, as in the sultanate-of-gowa dossier, which files the same relation (ledger 1626 and 1667) against the free string 'Sumbawa' and should name sultanate-of-bima instead.

region.text: the Sumbawa part of Cliopatria's 1626 outline: Bima and the eastern end of the island, without the Flores tribute lands

ledger.note: 1667: Makassar loses Sumbawa. 'the Makassar empire was soundly defeated by the Dutch East India Company (VOC) in 1667 and again in 1669. As a consequence the Makassarese formally lost their vast possessions in eastern Indonesia, including their suzerainty over Sumbawa.' The page gives no year for the loss itself; 1667 is the first defeat (and the infobox's 'Suzerainty to Dutch East India Company: 1667'). Bima's own surrender is 8 December 1669 (next event).

region.text: the Sumbawa part of Cliopatria's 1626 outline: Bima and the eastern end of the island, without the Flores tribute lands

ledger.note: 8 December 1669: Bima surrenders to the VOC. 'The Bima Sultanate surrendered to the VOC on 8 December 1669 with an agreement signed in Batavia'; Bima and the other Sumbawan kingdoms were then 'subordinated allies of the VOC', 'a Dutch posthouder was placed close to the sultan's court', and a sappanwood export monopoly was enforced to 1874. The infobox has 'Suzerainty to Dutch East India Company: 1667', the year of Makassar's first defeat; the dated surrender is 1669. The page lists no terms and no cession; the Flores tributaries are not said to change hands.

ledger.note: 31 December 1799: the VOC's rule ends. Dutch East Indies page: infobox 'Direct Dutch control: 31 December 1799'; 'The company was formally dissolved in 1800 and its colonial possessions ... nationalized'. The Bima page is silent on 1799/1800; the dependence does not end but passes to dutch-east-indies in the next event (Cliopatria's Dutch Republic row ends in 1795 and its Dutch East Indies row starts in 1800, with the Batavian Republic of 1796-1810 between; the three share one colour in colours.json).

ledger.note: 1800: the Dutch state takes over the VOC's possessions: the colony 'came under the administration of the Dutch government in 1800' (Dutch East Indies page). The Bima page names no act between 1669 and 1905 except the sappanwood monopoly to 1874 and its succession box lists 'Dutch East Indies' without a date, so the continuing dependence is a reading (confidence 2); Cliopatria's Dutch East Indies shape already covers part of eastern Sumbawa from 1800. The British occupation of Java from 1811 (same page) is not on the Bima page and is not modelled.

wars.name: Makassar's expeditions against Sumbawa
wars.outcome: Makassar attacked Sumbawa in 1618, 1619 and 1626 (the page's years). Bima signed 'a contract of alliance with Makassar' (no year) and its Sultan Abu'l-Khair Sirajuddin 'assisted Makassar in warfare outside Sumbawa'; a rebellion against Makassarese-backed rule followed in 1632-33.
wars.note: The sultanate-of-gowa dossier carries the contest and vassal events for Sumbawa; the page does not call Bima a vassal. The relation is now mirrored in this ledger (vassal_start 1626, vassal_end 1667, counterpart sultanate-of-gowa).

wars.name: VOC subjugation of Bima
wars.outcome: The VOC defeated Makassar in 1667 and 1669 and the Makassarese 'formally lost... their suzerainty over Sumbawa'; 'The Bima Sultanate surrendered to the VOC on 8 December 1669 with an agreement signed in Batavia', after which Bima was a 'subordinated ally of the VOC' with a Dutch posthouder near the court and a sappanwood export monopoly to 1874.
wars.note: The page lists no terms and no land cession. The surrender of 8 December 1669, signed in Batavia, is ledger vassal_start (counterpart dutch-republic, confidence 3); the infobox gives 'Suzerainty to Dutch East India Company: 1667'.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary; the Sumbawa core is Cliopatria's outline, and the Flores tribute lands are a tint of uncertain extent.

notes: One page was opened (twice, with two questions; budget 1-2). Cliopatria's three rows (1626-1865, 1866-1884, 1885-1889) are one outline with a smaller one from 1866 that loses the Bima plain itself; the page has no sentence for 1866, 1885 or 1889 and the 1866 shape is not used. The 1626 outline includes Komodo and Manggarai on Flores, which the page treats as tradition-based tributary dependencies; the dossier keeps Sumbawa as Bima's land and records Flores as a tributary (confidence 1 at the start; the page's 1920 for the loss of Manggarai lies after the dossier's end, so the tributary ends with the state in 1905). The dossier ends in 1905 (the fief), not Cliopatria's 1889; the sultanate lasted to 1958 and Bima was a VOC 'subordinated ally' from 1669, which this ledger now carries as vassal events (see the fix pass below). Later events on the page, outside the dossier: Sanggar merged with Bima in 1928, Dompu incorporated under the Japanese and handed back after 1945, the Tambora eruption of 1815 (disaster and famine), joining East Indonesia in December 1946. The Bima gazetteer entries are missing; Sumbawa and Flores are not in the gazetteer, so regions use Cliopatria's outline and the Nusa Tenggara Timur province as the cut between Sumbawa and Flores. Reviewer-fix pass (se-02-g, 2026-10-19): added the VOC subordination (vassal_start 8 December 1669, dutch-republic, confidence 3; the Bima page; the infobox says 'Suzerainty to Dutch East India Company: 1667', the dated surrender is 1669), its handover to dutch-east-indies in 1800 (vassal_end 31 December 1799 and vassal_start 1800, both from the Dutch East Indies page, because the Bima page is silent on the VOC's end; confidence 2) and the end of that dependence at the 1905 fief; added the mirror of the Gowa dossier's Sumbawa relation (vassal_start 1626 and vassal_end 1667, counterpart sultanate-of-gowa, confidence 2; the Gowa dossier still uses the free string 'Sumbawa' at its ledger 8 and 16 and should use sultanate-of-bima). The 1920 loss of Manggarai was already moved to 1905 by the reviewer (the event is outside the life; the tributary is a bridge, confidence 2). Thin items: the start of the Flores/Sumba tribute is still undated (the Manggarai Regency page was opened and is silent on Bima; the Bima page says only 'according to tradition' and a 15th-century peak); the 1866 shrinkage of Cliopatria's outline has no page and the core is kept. The VOC period 1669-1799 is drawn on the Sumbawa core only, because the page names no Dutch act on Flores. The Dutch East Indies page was a second page (budget 1-2); the Manggarai Regency page a third, silent one.
